Q: Instagram OAuth not working — "Sorry, this page isn't available" fix A:

The question is why this happens:

The Meta Business Login Guide requires the www subdomain for user authorization. However, the legacy documentation incorrectly listed api.instagram.com for both steps. Meta recently enforced this separation strictly:

  • For Authorization: Must use www.instagram.com to safely present the login UI to the user.

  • For Token Exchange: Must continue using https://instagram.com for your back-end server-to-server POST request.

Q: Spring - Multiple Spring Data modules found, entering strict repository configuration mode A:

Here is the actual, deep reason why is it happening. Let me explain everything in order to let you understand the guts (be ready, it will be quite long and comprehensive). If you are looking for simple solution, go to the bottom of my answer:

First of all, the Spring Framework data, as a general module (forget about particular modules, like Spring Data JPA, or Spring Data Redis), has an hierarchy of interfaces. It begins from Repository, then comes CrudRepository, and after that there is PagingAndSortingRepository.

I will not get into details about the difference between them; this is not the point now. What is important - these interfaces are absolutely segregated from the particular persistence storage, just because they are technically resides within the separate JAR that ships right away with any particular spring data implementation (it is called spring-data-commons, see official documentation, if you are interested).

I mean: You can use a Spring data module for MongoDB. In order to take advantage of Spring data MongoDB what would you typically do: Right, extend the CrudRepository, or Repository or MongoRepository. It is very important - from the spring-data perspective, if you create your own interface by extending Repository, or CrudRepository and you did not marked the target repository entity anyhow (I will explain at the end of the answer), then Spring will basically try to find out by itself, how exactly this magical methods: findById, deleteById and etc. must by implemented, because obviously their implementation will be different in Mongo and in JPA. With this in mind, read on.

The question is - how exactly does Spring determine the way you custom interfaces must be implemented? Well, there is an abstraction within the Spring guts, called RepositoryFactoryBeanSupport. This is the thing that actually participate in beans creation from your custom repositories. Let’s make an experiment now: Try out add both Spring data JDBC starter and Spring data MongoDB starter into your project. You will notice, that in your classpath there are two different implementations of RepositoryFactoryBeanSupport:

  1. JdbcRepositoryFactoryBean (comes from the Spring data JDBC starter)
  2. MongoRepositoryFactoryBean (comes from the Spring data MongoDB starter)

Then, let’s assume, that I have an entity, like this:

@AllArgsConstructor
@NoArgsConstructor
@Data
public class Customer {

    @Id
    private Long id;

    @Column("firstname")
    private String firstName;

    @Column("phone")
    private String phone;
}

Also note: The Id and the Column annotations are actually Spring data annotations, not JPA.

Then let’s define an interface (simple DAO interface):

public interface CustomerCRUDRepository extends CrudRepository<Customer, Long> {
    int countByFirstName(String firstName);
}

And now, inject the bean of type CustomerCRUDRepository somewhere. Just try to bootstrap the application; you will fail. Why? Let’s investigate the logs together:

RepositoryConfigurationDelegate : Multiple Spring Data modules found, entering strict repository configuration mode!

RepositoryConfigurationDelegate : Bootstrapping Spring Data JDBC repositories in DEFAULT mode

RepositoryConfigurationExtensionSupport : Spring Data JDBC - Could not safely identify store assignment for repository candidate interface com.example.springdatajdbc.repositories.CustomerCRUDRepository

The same exception as in your question, is not it? Let us finally break this down. Now let me finally answer the question.

So, why does this exception appear?

When you, having multiple Spring-data modules within a project, try to create an interface for specific entity, that does not annotated with specific to persistence technology annotation (like @Entity in javax.persistence, or @Document in case of MongoDB, you name it), by extending the interface from spring-data-commons module (i.e., Repository or CrudRepository). This will not work at all, because Spring doesn't basically have any idea, to which exactly data storage you entity is associated. Is it MongoDB? Or is it JPA? Or Cassandra? It is impossible to determine in that way; see the official documentation. On the other hand, when there is only one Spring data module in classpath, Spring can conclude all by itself, because it is not ambiguous.

What can you do to solve it

  1. Extend the technology-specific repository. For example, if you want entity A to be associated with PostgreSQL, then do not use CrudRepository; use JpaRepository. If you want entity B to be associated with Redis, then use RedisRepository and so on.

  2. Annotate your entity with an annotation. That indicates its affiliation to the specific data storage. @Entity, @Document, @Table and so on.

I hope this is clear now. I really did my best to explain it to you. Thanks for reading; have a nice day!

Q: How to distinguish an OpenAI API "quota exceeded" 429 from a standard rate limit 429? A:

openai.RateLimitError` is raised for both cases. The HTTP response body contains an `error.code` field that tells you which limit was hit.

```python

from openai import RateLimitError

try:

resp = client.chat.completions.create(...)

except RateLimitError as e:

# e.response is an httpx.Response

payload = e.response.json()

code = payload.get("error", {}).get("code")

if code == "insufficient_quota":

# Account‑level spend cap reached.

# Upgrade plan or wait for next billing period.

raise

elif code == "rate_limit_exceeded":

# Per‑minute request or token limit reached.

# Safe to retry after a back‑off.

retry_after = e.response.headers.get("retry-after")

# implement back‑off logic here

else:

# Unknown error code.

raise

```

`insufficient_quota` means the account‑level quota is exhausted; the request cannot succeed until the quota is increased. `rate_limit_exceeded` means a transient per‑minute or per‑token limit was hit, and a retry after the indicated delay may succeed. The `message` string is not stable, so rely on the `code` field.

Q: How can I find a specific consecutive sequence of rows in SQL without MATCH_RECOGNIZE? A:

TL;DR

The final query is in the section "Using pure ANSI SQL features" at the bottom.

How to achieve it step by step

The following is testing on my SQL Server express edition. Let's first try to create the test data:

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS CRIMES; -- for regression tests
GO

CREATE TABLE CRIMES (
    ID       BIGINT IDENTITY(1, 1) PRIMARY KEY,
    TS       DATETIME     NOT NULL DEFAULT GETDATE(),
    TYPE     NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    DISTRICT INT          NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('ROBBERY');
WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00.1';
INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('ASSAULT');
WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00.1';
INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('ROBBERY');
WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00.1';
INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('BATTERY');
WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00.1';
INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT');
WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00.1';
INSERT CRIMES(TYPE) VALUES('DOMESTIC');
GO

-- see how the raw data is created
SELECT   *
FROM     CRIMES
ORDER BY TS;

The result is:

(1 row affected)
ID                   TS                      TYPE                 DISTRICT
-------------------- ----------------------- -------------------- -----------
1                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.747 ROBBERY              0
2                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.860 ASSAULT              0
3                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.033 ROBBERY              0
4                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.140 BATTERY              0
5                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.317 MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT  0
6                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.440 DOMESTIC             0

Now we try to apply LEAD() to get subsequent types from rows in current rows.

SELECT   *,
         NEXT_1 = LEAD(TYPE, 1) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
         NEXT_2 = LEAD(TYPE, 2) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
         NEXT_3 = LEAD(TYPE, 3) OVER (ORDER BY TS)
FROM     CRIMES
ORDER BY TS;

Result from applying LEAD():

ID                   TS                      TYPE                 DISTRICT    NEXT_1               NEXT_2               NEXT_3
-------------------- ----------------------- -------------------- ----------- -------------------- -------------------- --------------------
1                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.747 ROBBERY              0           ASSAULT              ROBBERY              BATTERY
2                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.860 ASSAULT              0           ROBBERY              BATTERY              MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT
3                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.033 ROBBERY              0           BATTERY              MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT  DOMESTIC
4                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.140 BATTERY              0           MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT  DOMESTIC             NULL
5                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.317 MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT  0           DOMESTIC             NULL                 NULL
6                    2026-08-22 16:14:40.440 DOMESTIC             0           NULL                 NULL                 NULL

Now we try get the row(s) which type sequence matches [ASSAULT -> ROBBERY -> BATTERY -> MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT] using CTE (Common Table Expression):

WITH WINDOW_CTE AS (
    SELECT ID, TS, TYPE, DISTRICT,
           NEXT_1 = LEAD(TYPE, 1) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_2 = LEAD(TYPE, 2) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_3 = LEAD(TYPE, 3) OVER (ORDER BY TS)
    FROM   CRIMES
)
SELECT   ID, TS, TYPE, DISTRICT
FROM     WINDOW_CTE
         -- ASSAULT -> ROBBERY -> BATTERY -> MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT
         -- CURRENT -> NEXT_1  -> NEXT_2  -> NEXT_3
WHERE    TYPE   = 'ASSAULT'
     AND NEXT_1 = 'ROBBERY'
     AND NEXT_2 = 'BATTERY'
     AND NEXT_3 = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT'
ORDER BY TS;

Indeed it locates that. In our test data we have only 1 such group, which starts at ID=2:

ID                   TS                      TYPE                 DISTRICT
-------------------- ----------------------- -------------------- -----------
2                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.860 ASSAULT              0

In case we need to get all the IDs:

WITH WINDOW_CTE AS (
    SELECT ID, TS, TYPE, DISTRICT,
           NEXT_1    = LEAD(TYPE, 1) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_2    = LEAD(TYPE, 2) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_3    = LEAD(TYPE, 3) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_1 = LEAD(ID, 1)   OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_2 = LEAD(ID, 2)   OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_3 = LEAD(ID, 3)   OVER (ORDER BY TS)
    FROM   CRIMES
)
SELECT   ASSULT_ID  = ID,
         ROBBERY_ID = NEXT_ID_1,
         BATTERY_ID = NEXT_ID_2,
         THEFT_ID   = NEXT_ID_3,
         TS, TYPE, DISTRICT
FROM     WINDOW_CTE
WHERE    TYPE   = 'ASSAULT'
     AND NEXT_1 = 'ROBBERY'
     AND NEXT_2 = 'BATTERY'
     AND NEXT_3 = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT'
ORDER BY TS;

The result:

ASSULT_ID            ROBBERY_ID           BATTERY_ID           THEFT_ID             TS                      TYPE                 DISTRICT
-------------------- -------------------- -------------------- -------------------- ----------------------- -------------------- -----------
2                    3                    4                    5                    2026-08-22 16:14:39.860 ASSAULT              0

Final query (in T-SQL)

Now we need to add BATTERY time-stamp range constraint so it's between 1755864000 ~ 1755873000 (Unix epoch time) as you requested. Unix epoch time 1755864000 is 2025-08-22 12:00:00 and 1755873000 is 2025-08-22 14:30:00, so the actual query would not return any result from my test data which is created just a moment ago, not yesteryear. But it should work for you, in case you are also using SQL Server.

WITH WINDOW_CTE AS (
    SELECT ID, TS, TYPE, DISTRICT,
           NEXT_1    = LEAD(TYPE, 1) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_2    = LEAD(TYPE, 2) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_3    = LEAD(TYPE, 3) OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_1 = LEAD(ID, 1)   OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_2 = LEAD(ID, 2)   OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           NEXT_ID_3 = LEAD(ID, 3)   OVER (ORDER BY TS),
           -- ASSAULT -> ROBBERY -> [BATTERY] -> MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT
           -- CURRENT -> NEXT_1  -> [NEXT_2 ] -> NEXT_3
           TS_2      = LEAD(TS, 2)   OVER (ORDER BY TS)
    FROM   CRIMES
)
SELECT   ASSULT_ID  = ID,
         ROBBERY_ID = NEXT_ID_1,
         BATTERY_ID = NEXT_ID_2,
         THEFT_ID   = NEXT_ID_3,
         TS, TYPE, DISTRICT
FROM     WINDOW_CTE
WHERE    TYPE   = 'ASSAULT'
     AND NEXT_1 = 'ROBBERY'
     AND NEXT_2 = 'BATTERY'
     AND NEXT_3 = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT'
     AND TS_2 BETWEEN DATEADD(SECOND, 1755864000, '1970-01-01') AND DATEADD(SECOND, 1755873000, '1970-01-01')
ORDER BY TS;

Using pure ANSI SQL features

We can get rid of DATEADD() because it's not in ANSI SQL. Maybe CTE should also be replaced because major vendors supported it since 1999 (MySQL since version 8 only). So we can translate the solution back to ANSI SQL format, on the ground that the TS column has the LONG time to keep Unix Epoch time directly:

SELECT ID        AS ASSULT_ID,
       NEXT_ID_1 AS ROBBERY_ID,
       NEXT_ID_2 AS BATTERY_ID,
       NEXT_ID_3 AS THEFT_ID,
       TS, TYPE, DISTRICT
FROM (
    SELECT 
        ID, TS, TYPE, DISTRICT,
        LEAD(TYPE, 1) OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_1,
        LEAD(TYPE, 2) OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_2,
        LEAD(TYPE, 3) OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_3,
        LEAD(ID, 1)   OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_ID_1,
        LEAD(ID, 2)   OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_ID_2,
        LEAD(ID, 3)   OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS NEXT_ID_3,
        LEAD(TS, 2)   OVER (ORDER BY TS) AS TS_2
    FROM CRIMES
) AS RUNNING_WINDOW
WHERE TYPE   = 'ASSAULT'
  AND NEXT_1 = 'ROBBERY'
  AND NEXT_2 = 'BATTERY'
  AND NEXT_3 = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT'
  AND TS_2 BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000
ORDER BY TS;

Q: ___tmp___/punish? in response A:

I kept getting that rgv587_flag sm payload and it just means their risk engine tossed the request. Happens when you hammer too fast, use a datacenter ip, sit on old cookies or your tls and headers look weird. Residential ip plus a real browser handshake cut the challenges down but they will not run the sensor js for you once you are already intercepted. When the official api does not have the catalog fields I use undetected chromedriver or playwright stealth and wiggle the slider. Then I pull the new x5sec cookie from the browser and drop it into my http client until the session dies

Q: pod install Xcode Error Failed to save foo.xcodeproj A:

This issue occurs when Xcode detects external changes while it already has drafted changes. The most common situations I personally encounter are:

  • Having multiple instances of Xcode opened on the same project (usually different versions, such as Xcode 15 and Xcode 16).
  • Applying discard, pull, merge, or other changes in Git outside of Xcode.
  • Modifying a file using a script, such as with the terminal.

My solution to these issues is as follows:

  • Keep all the tech stack up to date to the latest stable version (Xcode, macOS)
  • Ensure only one instance of Xcode is running at a time.
  • Close Xcode before applying any external changes, and reopen it afterward.
  • Ensure there is no ongoing process (like a process in terminal or background) when using Xcode.
  • Always use git as the source of truth for changes (Xcode has wiped out my changes many times, and I don’t trust it anymore).

Hope it helps ( And hope Apple fix these obvious frustrating issues some day :) )

Q: Why does Keycloak use a Session-Cookie instead of JWT Authorization Header A:

You write:

When I want to access a protected resource I am shown the Keycloak login form and can log in. I get redirected to the resource after login.

This leads me to assume you're using a browser and issuing a GET request. I'm assuming the browser is using the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant Type, and so the tokens are exchanged between the client (the web server) and the Keycloak server. And not between the web browser and the web server. This is a decision that was made by the team developing the "protected resource" and not something you can change without changing the source code of the "protected resource".

You also write:

In the request header I can see that the header Cookie: mongo-express=s%3AVpTxrBrZp_bb1kpZOuCo6nitgpTzI0YJ.6OS1ttu4hjcnut%2FG6zdyDnLk2B%2FrEmMEEw9jy2rCUrE; SESSION=510eb294-493e-4cb6-9cb8-1e09604a7fc7 is set.

If you start a browser form scratch (or use e.g. "New Incognito Window" in Chrome or "New Private Window" in Firefox) I'm pretty sure you'll see that in the response to the very first GET request to the protected resource, you'll find a Set-Cookie HTTP header in the server response (presumably the one that redirects to the OAuth2 server). This is just how the protected resource manages its sessions. Not much you can do about that, I'm affraid.
